items.title: Localising a localised module twice gives the localisation at the product set
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file algebra.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The proposition states that for multiplicative subsets S and S' of a ring A and an A-module M, the iterated localisation of M at S after S' is isomorphic to the localisation at the product subset (statement lines 1518-1522). The proof does not cite a universal property: the author explicitly notes that none has been proved for module localisation at this point, and therefore writes the isomorphism down on fractions, giving both directions and their decomposition of a denominator as a product, then noting that well-definedness and the inverse property are easy checks (proof lines 1524-1541). Constructing the two maps on elements, rather than deducing the result from a universal property, is the substance; the author's sentence about the omitted routine checks is kept verbatim inside the span. H2.
